chunks: Ali ibn Ibrahim, from his father, from Ibn Abi Umeyr, from Abu Ayoub, from Muhammad ibn Muslim and others, said:

I asked Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) about a man who borrows a loan from another man and gives him a pledge, whether a servant, or a utensil, or clothes. So he (the lender) needs something from its benefit, so he seeks permission from the borrower to use it, and the borrower permits him. He (peace be upon him) said: 'If he is pleased with it, there is no problem.' I said: 'Those among us narrate that every loan that brings a benefit is invalid.' He (peace be upon him) said: 'Is it not the case that the best of loans is that which brings a benefit?'

key_terms.طَابَتْ نَفْسُهُ: He was pleased / His soul agreed

ai.seo_question: Is it permissible for a lender to use the pledged item as benefit from a loan in Shia jurisprudence?
ai.summary: This hadith from al-Kafi addresses the juristic debate regarding 'qard al-mutatabbi' (loan with benefit), where Imam al-Sadiq (AS) validates deriving benefit from a pledged item (rahn) if the lender consents, countering the view that any benefit invalidates the loan. He elevates this practice by citing the Prophetic tradition that 'the best loan is that which brings benefit,' thereby distinguishing permissible mutual benefit from usurious riba. This ruling highlights the Shia scholarly emphasis on the lender's voluntary consent and the practical utility of collateral in commercial transactions.
